candidates.visible_reason: On the top tie, the surface around and below the plate seat looks broken up. Wood layers are peeling and splintered, with a cavity-like dark hollow and loose slivers or flaps near the lower centre-right. A thin piece of wood or metal sticks out from the splintered area.
candidates.uncertainty: Medium. The view is oblique and the rust staining makes it hard to tell surface splintering from deeper loss. The depth of the damage cannot be judged from one photo.
alternatives: Superficial surface delamination or weathering made to look worse by rust staining and shadow
Handling or stacking damage on a tie that is not in track
Debris or loose wood fragments resting on the surface

candidates.visible_reason: Around the plate seat area on the top tie, the wood is heavily rust-stained and the grain looks torn and layered. Several dark round holes and elongated dark voids sit along the surface, with open cracks running between them.
candidates.uncertainty: High. The round holes could be old spike or bolt holes. The cracks may be ordinary checking, and it is unclear whether the damage goes through the tie.
alternatives: Normal surface checking and rust staining from a removed tie plate
Dark shadowed areas that look like voids
